title: How Long Would You Last Falling Into a Black Hole? #shorts
description_hook: In a spacesuit, you start falling toward a black hole of 4.3 million solar masses, following NASA's plunge simulation. The clock starts now.

beats.say: How long would you last falling into a black hole? In a suit, you start 640 million kilometers out. It weighs 4.3 million solar masses.
beats.img: a lone astronaut silhouette seen from behind floating in deep space, facing a vast black sphere ringed by a thin glowing orange disk far ahead, cold starlight

beats.say: You don't drop straight in. Gravity swings you around it. One orbit every 30 minutes, tighter each time.
beats.img: a curved trail of light spiraling inward around a dark gravitational well, a tiny spacesuited figure riding the bright arc, swirling hot gas below

beats.say: About 3 hours in, you cross the event horizon, 25 million kilometers wide. You feel nothing special. There is no way back.
beats.img: the view looking down into a perfectly black edge filling the whole frame, starlight bent into a thin bright ring at the border, eerie calm

beats.say: In NASA's simulation, 12.8 seconds later, the tides stretch you like spaghetti. The center is still 128,000 kilometers away.
beats.img: a glowing outline of a human figure stretched into a long thin ribbon of light, pulled down into absolute darkness, distorted stars around it

gumi.say: Gumi's odds: zero. A small one of 8 solar masses shreds you 400 km out.
